correctness.rationale: Using Ferroni--Riccardi's interval-poset representation Q, rank-one elements are [vertex,1] and [0,facet], giving a1=v+f. Rank two consists of [edge,1], [0,edge] and vertex--facet incidences; the latter count is 2e, so a2=4e. For rank-three lower intervals, the local toric g linear coefficient is atoms-3. Summing over [facet,1] and [0,vertex] gives 4e-3(v+f), while the [edge,facet] and [vertex,edge] types contribute zero. In the toric h recursion this yields [x^3]h=v+f-4 and [x^2]h=6+8e-6(v+f). Euler's relation e=v+f-2 reduces the latter to 2(v+f)-10; toric h symmetry supplies the remaining coefficients. The factorization is direct. Since every three-polytope has v,f>=4, v+f-8>=0 and the quadratic factor has discriminant (v+f-8)(v+f-4)>=0 with positive coefficients, so its roots are negative. The finite verifier checks representative Platonic examples only as consistency tests.

final_claim: For every convex three-polytope with v vertices and f facets, the Eulerian-kernel Z-polynomial is (1+x)^2(x^2+(v+f-6)x+1), equivalently with coefficient vector (1,v+f-4,2v+2f-10,v+f-4,1); hence its gamma vector is (1,v+f-8,0) and it is gamma-positive and real-rooted.
